results.title: Tariffs could affect supply chains, SIU professor says
results.content:
“While the broad-based tariffs on imports to the U.S. have clearly had an unsettling effect on global stock markets,” he said, “we may experience some significant underlying effects as well, particularly on supply chain management. Supply chain activities don’t take place in a vacuum.”

DeYong said global trade negotiations are typically “both time-consuming and fickle,” so he anticipates that at least in the near future, consumers and businesses will experience volatility. [...] by Christi Mathis

CARBONDALE, Ill. — President Donald Trump’s tariffs ranging from 10% to 50% may have some very significant impacts on various manufacturing and supply chain management firms, said Gregory D. DeYong, a Southern Illinois University Carbondale associate professor of operations management, meaning both availability and pricing on a variety of products may be an up and down seesaw as talks go on. [...] And he said American farmers will be some of the first to experience immediate negative impacts as the demand for U.S. agricultural products weakens due to the tariffs as they have experienced before.
